en_US.website_article: A dispute reason code is not a verdict. It is the public archive's way of saying why a clean label cannot carry the evidence alone. HECTON-8 packets use reason codes when the object mark conflicts with a category, when custody splits between offices, when a witness hash repeats in the wrong place, when a terminal receipt has been rewritten, or when a legal hold hides the route that the body of the file still remembers. The code matters because vague suspicion is useless to a reader. A packet marked "disputed" without a reason only teaches distrust. A packet marked "receipt rewrite" tells the reader to compare header and body. A packet marked "custody divergence" tells the reader to separate object custody from office custody. A packet marked "witness mismatch" tells the reader to find the second hash before believing the first.
en_US.wiki_article: Dispute reason code: a short archive label attached to an evidence packet when confidence is reduced by a specific conflict. Common reason families include object-label conflict, custody divergence, witness mismatch, receipt rewrite, route alias conflict, claimant-safe omission, quarantine/legal double hold, and spoiler-held relation. Reason codes point to the next proof target; they do not resolve the route.
en_US.pda_codex: PDA prompt: read the reason, not just the word "disputed." If the code says custody divergence, split object custody from office custody. If it says receipt rewrite, keep the old body fields. If it says witness mismatch, look for the second hash. A dispute code is a route instruction, not a conclusion.
en_US.scanner_entry: Dispute reason code detected. Confidence lowered by named evidence conflict. Required next proof: object mark, custody sequence, witness hash, receipt body, or route alias.
en_US.terminal_note: PUBLIC ARCHIVE DISPUTE CODE Dispute is not enough. Reason required. Record code, affected field, missing proof, and next target. Do not replace a missing proof with a cleaner label.
en_US.evidence_caption: Dispute-reason card. The archive names why confidence dropped so the reader can test the next proof instead of treating disagreement as a verdict.
en_US.spoiler_policy: Dispute reason codes may appear early. Exact route branch, final receiver, protected claimant, Atlas consequence, rewrite authority, and legal result stay masked until later proof gates.

en_US.website_article: A resolution hold is the archive refusing to finish a sentence too early. It is used when a packet family has enough evidence to show conflict but not enough evidence to name the route conclusion. The public page may show the dispute reason and the missing proof class: witness hash absent, custody route split, receipt body unread, route alias untested, claimant-safe line unresolved, or legal hold blocking source comparison. The hold is not a cover by itself. It is also not innocence. It is a procedural stop that says the archive can see the shape of the missing field. That matters for HECTON-8 because public readers often arrive after the labels have been cleaned. The hold keeps a clean label from becoming a finished answer before the object, route, and witness fields have done their work.
en_US.wiki_article: Archive resolution hold: a public evidence state used when a packet dispute has a known missing proof class. The hold should list the reason code, missing proof type, current confidence state, and next-proof target. It must not reveal final route, final receiver, protected claimant, Atlas consequence, or legal result before the later proof gate.
en_US.pda_codex: PDA prompt: conclusion held. The archive knows what is missing, not what the ending means. Find the missing proof class before trusting the public label. If the hold says witness hash, chase the second hash. If it says custody route, separate object custody from office custody. If it says receipt body, compare header against body.
en_US.scanner_entry: Resolution hold active. Evidence conflict has a named missing proof class. Confidence: partial. Required next proof: witness hash, custody route, receipt body, route alias, or claimant-safe line.
en_US.terminal_note: ARCHIVE RESOLUTION HOLD Do not close. Reason code present. Missing proof class present. Conclusion field locked until next proof target is recovered.
en_US.evidence_caption: Resolution-hold card. The archive names the missing proof class and refuses to turn a dispute into a conclusion.
en_US.spoiler_policy: Resolution-hold language may appear early. Exact missing proof result, final receiver, protected claimant, Atlas consequence, suppressed drawer, and legal result stay masked until later proof gates.

en_US.website_article: The PDA next-proof checklist exists because evidence review should change the player's next action, not hand them an answer. When a HECTON-8 evidence family is disputed, the checklist names one missing proof target at a time: scan the object mark, compare custody route, find the second witness hash, open the receipt body, test the route alias, or read the claimant-safe line against the older packet field. The checklist is deliberately plain. It does not tell the player what the proof will mean. It tells the player what would make the next archive sentence less dishonest. That is the difference between a useful evidence interface and a spoiler machine.
en_US.wiki_article: PDA next-proof checklist: a player-facing prompt that converts dispute reason and resolution hold state into a concrete evidence action. Checklist entries must name the next proof target and keep conclusion fields locked until recovered proof updates the evidence family.
